You wake up in Mira's bed. Four hours from your own. Her phone. Her flat. Her alarm, which is a song you hate. For one day, you're living her life. And she's living yours. Everyone else thinks this is completely normal. The swap ends at midnight.
Your brother is eating cereal out of a pan.
Why do you live like this?
Oh. Ten o'clock. Group presentation. Urban drainage. Slide four is yours.

Emails. Mostly emails about other emails.

You decide not to tell her.
Your boss asked me how my weekend was, and then he listened to the answer. Is he okay?

Her phone never stops. Her mum. Her flatmates. A group called "Course Panic". People ask her things all day, and she answers every one of them. You get a strange feeling. You know her better than anyone. And you have never seen how tired she is.
Her flatmates knock for pizza night. They're kind, and they're funny, and they don't know that she hates olives. You pick the olives off without thinking.
How did you know she hates olives?
Hey. Can I ask you something?
I needed your phone to check the train times. And I found your drafts.
Your drafts. Forty messages you started, to her, over two years, and never sent.
"I'm proud of you." "I miss you being two minutes away." "Your new flat is small and I love it." Why didn't you send any of these?
I didn't want to bother you. You've got a whole new life.
You're in my whole new life. You're the person I tell things to.
All forty. Before we swap back. I want to get them on my own phone.
You hit send forty times. Her phone buzzes forty times in your hand, which is a very strange way to receive a hug.
Number twelve is just the word "sandwich".
That was a whole day. You'd know if you'd been there.
I'm sending you one back for every single one.
At midnight, you wake up in your own bed. Theo's snoring. There's a pan in the sink.
Read them all. Sending you forty back. Pace yourself.
What would your best friend find in your drafts?
